question.problem:
Find the general solution to the equation

$$
\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}-6\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+13y=0.
$$
question.worked_solution:
Let $y={e}^{\lambda x}.$ Differentiating $y$ with respect to $x$ gives

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=\lambda {e}^{\lambda x},\,\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}={\lambda }^{2}{e}^{\lambda x}.
$$

Substituting the above into our differential equation gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{\lambda }^{2}{e}^{\lambda x}-6\lambda {e}^{\lambda x}+13{e}^{\lambda x} & =0 \\ {e}^{\lambda x}({\lambda }^{2}-6\lambda +13) & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

The auxiliary equation is therefore

$$
{\lambda }^{2}-6\lambda +13=0.
$$

The auxiliary equation can be solved by completing the square:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\lambda }^{2}-6\lambda +13 & =0 \\ ({\lambda }^{2}-6\lambda +9)-9+13 & =0 \\ (\lambda -3)^{2}+4 & =0 \\ (\lambda -3)^{2} & =-4 \\ \lambda -3 & =\pm 2\text{i} \\ \lambda  & =3\pm 2\text{i}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the general solution to the differential equation is

$$
\begin{aligned}y & ={e}^{3x}(P\operatorname{cos}⁡2x+Q\operatorname{sin}⁡2x).\end{aligned}
$$
